name: The AI Enablement Audit
title: The AI Enablement Audit
answer: The AI Enablement Audit maps every AI system an organization uses, pilots, or is likely to adopt, including image, video, audio, and text tools. It covers both internal models and third party services, from a single user's experimental account to enterprise wide deployments. The audit looks at who can access each system, what data flows into and out of it, and where AI output enters finished work. It treats enablement as a security and operations question, not just a productivity question.

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit maps every AI system an organization uses, pilots, or is likely to adopt, including image, video, audio, and text tools. It covers both internal models and third party services, from a single user's experimental account to enterprise wide deployments. The audit looks at who can access each system, what data flows into and out of it, and where AI output enters finished work. It treats enablement as a security and operations question, not just a productivity question.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The audit runs on the organization's existing identity, network, and cloud infrastructure, plus a lightweight discovery layer that inventories model endpoints, API keys, and local installations. It typically uses log aggregation, configuration management databases, and software asset registers to find AI usage that is not formally approved. No new model training or large compute is required; the audit is a review and measurement exercise. The infrastructure must support read only access to usage logs, permission groups, and data storage locations.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done in four passes: discovery, classification, risk scoring, and remediation planning. Discovery finds AI tools through expense records, browser extensions, API traffic, and interviews with creative and technical staff. Classification tags each tool by data sensitivity, model type, and business purpose. Risk scoring weighs security exposure, copyright and provenance risk, and operational dependence. The final pass produces a prioritized enablement plan that keeps low risk tools available while containing or replacing high risk ones.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk are treated as first class audit criteria, not legal afterthoughts. The audit checks training data provenance, model license terms, and whether outputs can be used commercially without infringing third party rights. It flags tools with unclear or contested ownership, including the 18 active lawsuits involving AI music services tracked by this site. The audit also records who approved each tool, what data it was allowed to see, and how outputs are labeled or stored, so that provenance can be reconstructed later.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The audit is moving from a one time project to a continuous control, with automated discovery and risk scoring updated as new models and tools appear. Organizations are beginning to require model cards, data flow diagrams, and usage telemetry as standard parts of procurement. The goal is not to block AI but to make its use visible, reversible, and defensible. Over time, enablement audits will likely merge with software supply chain security and content provenance tracking.
